text: Scene 7 The Theatre
speaker: C5

text: For some reason the house was crowded that night. The youths in the gallery talked to each other across the theatre
speaker: C6

text: Some women were laughing in the pit. and shared their oranges with the tawdry girls who sat beside them.
speaker: C8

text: Their voices were horribly shrill and discordant.
speaker: C5

text: The manager, beaming an oily tremulous smile, escorted them to their box with a sort of pompous humility.
speaker: C6

text: What a place to find one's divinity in!
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Yes! It was here I found her, and she is divine beyond all living things. When she acts, you will forget everything. These common rough people, with their coarse faces and brutal gestures, become quite different when she is on the stage. They sit silently and watch her. They weep and laugh as she wills them to do and one feels that they are of the same flesh and blood as one's self.
speaker: Dorian

text: The same flesh and blood as one's self! Oh, I hope not!
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Don't pay any attention to him, I understand what you mean, and I believe in this girl. Any one you love must be marvellous.
speaker: Basil

text: Thank you Basil, I knew that you would understand me. Harry is so cynical. But here is the orchestra. It is quite dreadful, but it only lasts for about five minutes. Then the curtain rises, and you will see the girl to whom I am going to give all my life, to whom I have given everything that is good in me.
speaker: Dorian

text: My only love sprung from my only hate! Too early seen unknown, and known too late! Prodigious birth of love it is to me, That I must love a loathed enemy
speaker: Sibyl

text: O, swear not by the moon, the innocent moon, That monthly changes in her cycled orb, Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.
speaker: Sibyl

text: O Romeo, Romeo! Wherefore art thou Romeo? Deny thy father and refuse his name; Or, if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love, And I’ll no longer be a Capulet.
speaker: Sibyl

text: She is quite beautiful, but she can't act. I cannot sit through another moment. Let us go.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: I am going to see the play through. I am awfully sorry that I have made you waste an evening, I apologise to you both.
speaker: Dorian

text: My dear Dorian, I should think Miss Vane was ill. We will come some other night.
speaker: Basil

text: I wish she were ill. But she seems to me to be simply callous and cold. She has entirely altered. Last night she was a great artist. This evening she is merely a commonplace mediocre actress.
speaker: Dorian

text: Don’t talk like that about any one you love. Love is a more wonderful thing than art.
speaker: Basil

text: They are both simply forms of imitation. But do let us go. Dorian - you must not stay here any longer. It is not good for one's morale to see bad acting. Besides, I don't suppose you will want your wife to act, so what does it matter if she plays Juliet like a wooden doll? She is very lovely, and if she knows as little about life as she does about acting, she will be a delightful experience.
speaker: Lord Henry

text: Go away, both of you I want to be alone. Can’t you see my heart is breaking.
speaker: Dorian
